subject.title: [Bug]: Secret provider crash-loop exhausts 1Password service account rate limits

question: Should OpenClaw change gateway startup SecretRef failures from pure fail-fast to a bounded retry/degrade policy for side-effecting exec providers under process supervisors?
rationale: The current behavior is deliberate fail-closed secret activation, but the reported failure mode can exhaust external credential-provider quotas across an account; choosing the retry, degrade, or documentation-only path is a security/product policy decision.

options.title: Add bounded generic startup protection
options.body: Implement provider-agnostic startup retry/backoff or restart-storm protection with tests and operator-visible logs, without hardcoding 1Password-specific behavior.

options.title: Keep fail-fast and document supervisor controls
options.body: Preserve the current startup security contract and add clear launchd/systemd restart-limit guidance plus external resolver recommendations.

options.title: Require explicit retry policy config
options.body: Add a narrow `secrets` retry/circuit-breaker config surface so operators opt into retry semantics per deployment.

recommendation.title: Add bounded generic startup protection
recommendation.body: Implement provider-agnostic startup retry/backoff or restart-storm protection with tests and operator-visible logs, without hardcoding 1Password-specific behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is closest to the external secrets/SecretRef runtime ownership shown in the feature history.
